source.paraphrase: The server directory runs only on the server. App code reaches it through routes, never through imports.

invariants.why: Importing server modules into app code bundles server-only dependencies into the client and leaks secrets and database handles.
invariants.fixHint: Expose the server logic through a server route or move the shared piece to a framework-agnostic util both sides may import.
invariants.avoid: Lazy import() does not fix the boundary. A dynamic import of a server module still ships it to the client.

source.paraphrase: readBody returns the raw payload. readValidatedBody parses it against a schema and rejects what does not fit.

invariants.why: An unshaped payload flows into database writes and business logic, so one malformed request corrupts state instead of failing at the boundary.
invariants.fixHint: Call readValidatedBody with a schema parse function and handle the validation error it throws.
invariants.avoid: A size limit is not validation. maxBodySize caps bytes but proves nothing about the payload shape.

source.work: Nuxt data fetching and Nitro proxy
source.locator: relative API paths in app code
source.paraphrase: App code calls same-origin APIs with relative paths. The Nitro server proxies them, so client and SSR agree on the origin.

invariants.why: An absolute URL pins an origin that differs between SSR, preview, and production, and it bypasses the Nitro proxy and its headers.
invariants.fixHint: Replace the origin with a relative path such as /api/orders and let Nitro route it.
invariants.avoid: Loopback is still an absolute origin. http://localhost works on one machine and breaks everywhere else.

source.paraphrase: The event object lives for one request. Exporting it lets later requests observe or mutate earlier request state.

invariants.why: A shared event binding leaks headers, sessions, and locals across requests, so one user sees another user's scope.
invariants.fixHint: Keep the event inside the handler closure and pass only plain values to helpers.
invariants.avoid: Renaming the binding to context does not change its scope. An exported alias leaks the same request.

source.work: Nuxt documentation, createError utility and server error handling (https://nuxt.com/docs/api/utils/create-error)
source.paraphrase: In server routes and middleware, throw createError({ statusCode, statusMessage }) to trigger H3 error handling; returning the error object does not reject the request.

invariants.why: Returning createError() from a Nitro handler serializes the error object as a normal response instead of halting middleware execution and sending the HTTP error status.
invariants.fixHint: Replace return createError(...) with throw createError(...).
invariants.avoid: Only return statements in server/** or src/server/** whose returned expression is a direct createError(...) call are flagged. Throwing createError(...) or passing it to a helper is allowed.
